cohort: Neonates admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) with a clinical diagnosis of neonatal sepsis, including those with culture-positive sepsis or clinical sepsis with a positive septic screen, as well as neonates suspected of having sepsis but with negative blood cultures and sepsis screens.
finding: Platelet count was lower and MPV was significantly higher in neonates with sepsis compared to the control group.
mod_finding: Neonatal sepsis was more common among vaginally delivered neonates (81.03%) compared to those delivered by C-section (11.29%).
